kevin (DevEx): Heads-up: found a weird edge when importing an old config to the new redwoodctl format. Import tool wrote duplicate profiles with different keys and broke login mapping.

kevin (DevEx): Steps: ran `redwoodctl config migrate --from v0.18` which created profiles `staging` and `staging-legacy` but also left an entry `Staging` in the flat config. Login `redwoodctl login --profile Staging` then tries device code but picks the wrong endpoint (legacy) intermittently.

rita (Platform): do you have the pre/post config snippets? curious about key collisions during migration.

kevin (DevEx): pre-migrate had a profile named `Staging` and a nested legacy key under `accounts.staging` that was imported as `staging-legacy`. After migration config looks like:
```
[profiles]
Staging = { endpoint = "https://staging.redwood.ai" }
staging-legacy = { endpoint = "https://old.staging.redwood.ai" }
[accounts]
staging = { last_used = 162345 }
```

omar (QA): Hmm. Could be our lookup code checks both profiles and accounts maps without a deterministic precedence. If ordering is nondeterministic, you get flakiness.

rita (Platform): Agreed. We should canonicalize resolution: check exact profile name in profiles first, then fallback to accounts.*, and warn if multiple candidates found. Also migration should not create names that only differ by case or suffix.

kevin (DevEx): Another problem: login picks the token cache by searching cache directory for substring `staging` and picks the first match. Because of the suffix `-legacy` the string matches both. That's why endpoint mismatches.

rita (Platform): That's a bug. Cache lookup must be exact key match, not substring. We should switch to strict filename mapping or the hashed filename approach. Also migration should populate a mapping file `cache/map.v1` so old tokens don't get orphaned.

omar (QA): I'll add a test: migrate sample config -> attempt login for both `Staging` and `staging-legacy` -> assert token resolution picks correct endpoint every time. Will run across mac/linux.

support-bot: telemetry: migrate.command=run, os=linux, version=0.23.0

kevin (DevEx): UX request: the migrate command prints a long JSON blob on stdout on success. Could we instead write a short summary and path to the full report file? The blob overwhelms terminal and users often miss the warning about name collisions.

rita (Platform): good call. We'll make migrate print a 3-line summary with counts and a path to `~/.redwood/migrate-report-<ts>.json` for details. Also add an explicit list of profile name collisions and suggested renames.

omar (QA): Also add a `--dry-run` for migrate so admins can preview renames and collisions.

kevin (DevEx): One more: during login after migrate, CLI shows `Authenticating...` spinner for a long time with no progress. Could we surface `using profile X -> endpoint Y` before starting auth so users see what it's trying to talk to?

rita (Platform): yep will add a one-line pre-auth log: `info: logging in using profile 'Staging' -> https://staging.redwood.ai` and improve cache lookup. I'll open a PR with migration guardrails and exact-match cache logic.

kevin (DevEx): Thanks. Workaround for folks: inspect `~/.redwood/config` and `~/.redwood/cache` after migration and rename duplicates before running login.
